name: ShaderScene
label: Shader scene
description: A WebGL2 scene, from a night horizon and a glowing rift to an aurora and a hearth of embers, in the theme's field colours, with fades, a vignette and grain.

props.name: scene
props.description: The scene to paint: `horizon`, a planet's limb at night, `rift`, a glowing tear, `glyphs`, soft light printed in type, `prism`, beams of light split into a spectrum, `meteors`, a shower over a planet's edge, `waves`, a rolling sea of points, `aurora`, ribbons of colour round a void, `dusk`, a soft dome of light low on black, or `embers`, sparks rising off a hearth.

props.name: params
props.description:
The scene's settings, merged over its defaults (`SHADER_SCENES` lists each
scene's keys and ranges), so passing one changes one thing. Changing them
never rebuilds the GL state.

props.name: passes
props.description:
The finishing passes (`scrim`, `vignette`, `fadeTop`, `fadeBottom`,
`grain`), each merged over its defaults.

props.name: speed
props.description: Scene seconds per second: how fast it moves. 0 holds it still.

props.name: liveRef
props.description:
A ref the scene reads every frame in place of `params`, `passes` and
`speed`, for a host that tunes it by drag: writing the ref moves the
scene and renders nothing. Empty falls back to the props.

props.name: pointerRef
props.description:
A ref the host writes the pointer into on every move, in client pixels,
or sets to null when the pointer leaves. The scene maps it onto its own
box and eases toward it each frame, so a move renders nothing. The scene
itself stays inert to pointer events; the host does the listening. Read
only while `pointerFollow` is above 0.

props.name: pointerFollow
props.description:
How strongly the scene answers the pointer: a broad swell round it,
rings running out from it while it moves, a slight lean toward it and a
lift of light under it. 0, the default, ignores the pointer; a value
near 0.3 is a subtle answer. Reduced motion turns it off.

props.name: enabled
props.description:
False never starts WebGL and reports `unavailable`, leaving the page
ground: the kill switch, as on ShaderField.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description:
Called whenever the status changes. Drive a fallback from this: the scene
paints only the page ground when it cannot run, and what to show instead
is the caller's design decision.
